high.title: After Months of Increases, Market Cuts 2026 Inflation Forecast; Focus Report for Monday (6)
high.summary:
The Banco Central do Brasil's weekly Focus Report — the closely watched survey of market expectations — shows that 2026 IPCA inflation projections declined for the first time in 16 consecutive weeks, easing marginally from 5.33% to 5.30%. This is a significant signal after an extended streak of upward revisions that had been pressuring the BRL and keeping rate-cut expectations firmly off the table. However, the relief is tempered: 2027 inflation expectations ticked up from 4.17% to 4.18%, and 2028–2029 estimates remained anchored at 3.70% and 3.50%, respectively — both still above the BCB's formal target. Critically, Selic rate projections were revised **upward** once again for 2026, reinforcing the market's view that the BCB will maintain its restrictive monetary stance well into the year. For BRL traders, the combination of a marginally lower near-term inflation print alongside a higher Selic path is a modestly constructive signal — higher-for-longer rates support carry dynamics. Bond investors should note that long-end yields may remain sticky given persistent above-target inflation in the medium-term horizon. Watch for any BCB communication that addresses whether this single-week decline in expectations marks a genuine turning point.

medium.title: Ibovespa: What to Expect from the Index in July and the Coming Quarters, According to BTG's Technical Analysis
medium.summary: July historically ranks among the most favorable months for the Ibovespa based on BTG Pactual's long-run dataset, combining positive average returns, a high frequency of monthly gains, and below-average volatility relative to other calendar months. This seasonal tailwind becomes particularly relevant in 2026 after the index lost momentum during Q2. BTG's technical analysis team notes the Ibovespa has accumulated a gain of approximately 6.76% year-to-date entering July. For international fund managers with Brazilian equity exposure, the seasonal pattern offers a constructive short-term setup, though it should be weighed against macro headwinds including the elevated Selic rate environment and any external risk-off pressures affecting emerging market flows. Investors should monitor whether technical support levels hold and whether domestic catalysts — particularly any COPOM guidance or fiscal developments — reinforce or undermine the seasonal bias heading into Q3.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4) Accounts for 65% of Federal State-Owned Enterprises' Profits — Is It Time to Invest?
medium.summary: Petrobras (PETR4) contributed R$110.6 billion of the R$169.4 billion in combined net profits reported by Brazil's 44 federal state-owned enterprises in 2025, representing approximately 65% of the total SOE result. The aggregate SOE profit figure represents a 45.4% increase year-over-year, according to data released by the Ministry of Management and Innovation (MGI). Empiricus maintains a positive outlook on the stock. For equity and macro investors, Petrobras remains a critical driver of Ibovespa performance, dividend flows, and government fiscal revenue — making its operational and political trajectory a key variable to monitor for both Brazilian equities and fiscal deficit dynamics.

medium.title: Itaú BBA Overhauls 80% of Recommended Stock Portfolio for July
medium.summary: Itaú BBA made sweeping changes to its monthly recommended equity portfolio for July, replacing Aura Minerals (AURA33), BTG Pactual (BPAC11), Equatorial (EQTL3), and Petrobras (PETR4) with Embraer (EMBJ3), Nubank (ROXO34), Sabesp (SBSP3), and Bradesco (BBDC4). The sole carry-over from June is Axia Energia (AXIA3). Notably, the June portfolio underperformed significantly, declining 4.5% versus a 1% drop in the Ibovespa — a 350 basis point underperformance. The inclusion of Bradesco (BBDC4) is relevant for banking sector watchers, as it signals Itaú BBA sees selective value in large-cap financials despite the high-rate environment. The rotation away from Petrobras in a major bank's model portfolio is worth monitoring as a sentiment indicator for the SOE.

medium.title: OECD Inflation Rises to 4.6% in May, Driven by Energy Prices
medium.summary: OECD-wide consumer inflation accelerated to 4.6% year-on-year in May 2026, up from 4.4% in April, with energy prices as the primary driver — rising sharply from 13.2% to 15.8% over the same period. Inflation accelerated in 16 member countries, decelerated in 8, and remained stable in 14. For Brazil-focused investors, elevated global inflation is a key external risk factor: it signals that major developed-market central banks (particularly the Fed and ECB) may maintain tighter monetary policy for longer, which could weigh on global risk appetite and emerging market capital flows, including those directed at Brazilian assets. Persistent global energy inflation also has direct pass-through implications for Brazil's own IPCA, particularly given Brazil's exposure to fuel and electricity price dynamics. This adds an external headwind to the BCB's already challenging inflation-management task and could reinforce the case for keeping the Selic elevated.

medium.title: Out-of-Court Restructurings Surge in Brazil Under Pressure from High Interest Rates
medium.summary: The high-profile out-of-court restructuring request filed by Raízen (RAIZ4), carrying R$65.1 billion in debt, has highlighted a broader trend: out-of-court restructuring filings in Brazil jumped from just 16 in 2021 to 84 in 2025, reflecting severe corporate stress driven by persistently elevated interest rates. This surge signals that prolonged restrictive monetary policy is beginning to generate meaningful credit stress across the Brazilian corporate sector. For fixed income and equity investors, this is an important systemic signal — rising corporate distress can increase non-performing loan ratios at major Brazilian banks (Itaú, Bradesco, Banco do Brasil), compress credit growth, and weigh on Ibovespa performance, particularly in leveraged sectors such as energy, agribusiness, and retail. It also reinforces the economic cost of the BCB's tight Selic stance and adds a layer of credit risk premium to monitor in Brazilian corporate bond spreads.

medium.title: Technology Stocks Divide Global Markets; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Advances 1% Today (6)
medium.summary:
The technology sector is once again driving global market sentiment this Monday (July 6), but with diverging impacts between East and West. Asian markets closed mostly lower, pressured by weak performance in technology-linked stocks, particularly in Japan and South Korea. In Tokyo, SoftBank — a conglomerate with heavy exposure to the artificial intelligence segment — fell 3.08%, while Tokyo Electron, a semiconductor equipment manufacturer, also declined. Notably, the article highlights that the **Ibovespa, measured in USD terms, advanced approximately 1%** on the day, a relevant data point for international fund managers as it signals BRL resilience or appreciation against the dollar alongside equity gains. This dual positive (equity + FX) dynamic is worth monitoring, as it may reflect improving risk appetite toward Brazilian assets or a broader EM rotation away from Asian tech. Investors should watch whether this USD-denominated Ibovespa strength is sustained and whether it is accompanied by inflows into Brazilian equities and BRL appreciation in spot FX markets.
